newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Brent bullish, again seeks upside gap.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Brent bullish, again seeks upside gap.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
+ Brent crude is bullish again in the short term and traders are likely to be aiming for the upside gap between $18.64 and $18.77.
+ Support at $17.54, $17.61 and $17.81 are strong bulwarks against any severe down move.
+ Gas oil is again well supported just below $160 a tonne.

IPE Brent crude oil futures are very well supported in the short to medium term and traders and technical analysts expected this base already built into the market will serve as a platform for strong gains on Friday.
June Brent closed 35 cents a barrel firmer at $18.41 on Thursday while May gas oil added $1.75 to end at $164.75.

"Now we have a good base in the market at $17.61," said Nicholas Wilson at MeesPierson Derivatives on the Isle of Man. That price is the eight-month low point formed on the June contract chart on April 17.
"The initial target is closure of the gap between $18.64 and $18.77 with a possible ultimate target centred on a previous consolidation range at around $19.25," Wilson said.

He expected this upside gap, (formed on April 2 and 3,) to be filled within the next couple of sessions. But in the longer term he was less optimistic. "I do not think the bear market is over. It is just time for a pause."

Al Graham at Elliott Wave International was bullish on Friday's Brent action, however. "At Thursday's close the candle is fully lit on this bull rocket. Strap yourself in on Friday and enjoy the wave," he said in his daily London report.
He cited nearby support for June Brent at $18.29-$18.35, then $18.03, and then "massive support" at $17.81.
This latter is a low reached on the June contract chart on April 23.
Gas oil is also well supported, Wilson said, with $159.75 as the key base level.
"There is a little bit of resistance up at $167.00 (the highest point of the recent consolidative range)and there is no reason it shouldn't move up to $170."
He said he saw a "little tight spot" based on earlier consolidation at between roughly $170 and $174.
"That is a reasonable short term target."
-- Nicholas Shaxson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8167
